abstract: The mRNA polyadenosine tail (pA-tail) is gradually shortened in the cytoplasm by two main deadenylase complexes, Ccr4-NOT and Pan2/3, eventually leading to decapping and decay. The yeast Ccr4-NOT complex contains two deadenylases, Ccr4 and Pop2, and seven non-catalytic subunits. The functions of the latter are not yet fully understood. Here, we investigate the role of Ccr4-NOT in RNA metabolism in budding yeast. We show that steady-state mRNA pA-tail lengths increase with growth temperature, with this effect enhanced in ccr4{Delta} and pop2{Delta} cells, indicating a role for Ccr4-NOT in temperature-dependent mRNA regulation. Consistent with a functional divergence between species, we confirm that Ccr4 is the predominant deadenylase in yeast, whereas the Pop2 orthologs CNOT7/8 are the major deadenylases in human cells. Using Illumina and direct RNA sequencing, we characterize yeast strains defective in Ccr4-NOT, Pan2/3, or mRNA decapping. Unexpectedly, we show that loss of NOT1, NOT2, NOT4 or POP2 causes transcriptome and pA-tail changes resembling those of the decapping-factor mutants dhh1{Delta} and lsm1{Delta}, rather than of the principal deadenylase mutant ccr4{Delta}, and induces a mild stress response. Loss of Not2 or Not4 prolongs the half-lives of several mRNAs and causes growth defects comparable to decapping co-factor mutants. The mRNAs stabilized by loss of Not1-2-4 are distinct from those preferentially deadenylated by Ccr4-Pop2, suggesting different substrate targeting by Ccr4-NOT for non-overlapping functions in deadenylation and decapping.

summary: Yeast Ccr4-NOT mutants link mRNA decapping rather than deadenylation to pA-tail changes, using Illumina and direct RNA sequencing of decay-pathway strains.
title: Mutations in core Ccr4-NOT subunits manifest links to decapping rather than deadenylation in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
